format: one-hour serialized prestige science-fiction political thriller / action drama
status: new series development package; pilot drafted; season architecture enhanced
premise: In the near-future megacity known as the Stack, Baseline Humans coexist uneasily with three posthuman classes: Organosynthetics grown alive without consent, Augmented Humans who rebuilt their bodies, and Artificial Intelligences developing independent agency. Engineered disasters and public incidents are used to blame, regulate and divide posthumans under the language of safety, stability and Pure Human supremacy. Organics, Augments and Intelligences are forced toward a fragile coalition while institutional power, private security interests and rogue Intelligence actors test whether they can be contained, rolled back or erased.
seriesThesis: This is not a story about becoming human. It is about who is allowed to count once humanity no longer means the same thing to everyone.
coreConflict: When identity outpaces governance, power responds with fear. The series asks whether solidarity across radically different forms of life can form before fear becomes permanent policy.
dramaticEngine: A civic or infrastructural crisis exposes a political boundary. Characters with incompatible identities and incentives must solve the immediate material problem together while institutions compete to define what the event means. Success can save lives and still worsen the political environment.
seriesPromise: Each story combines grounded future infrastructure, procedural problem-solving, political narrative warfare and intimate questions of bodily or cognitive autonomy. The spectacle is not that posthumans are powerful; it is that systems built to use their capabilities resist recognizing their agency.
themes: identity as emergent rather than fixed
politicalDoctrine: The antagonistic system works because legitimate institutions, private incentives, public fear and opportunistic actors reinforce one another; avoid reducing the conflict to one secret mastermind.

Pure Human politics should contain recognizable internal distinctions: true believers, frightened sympathizers, career opportunists, security institutionalists and people who adopt its language without embracing its full ideology.
Baseline Humans are not the enemy category. Baselines must appear throughout the Stack as allies, bystanders, beneficiaries, victims, opponents and people whose views change under pressure.
Posthuman groups contain real conflicts of interest. Coalition is meaningful precisely because their histories, bodies and political goals are not interchangeable.
Policy language should evolve from apparently neutral safety vocabulary toward explicit hierarchy. The migration of words is part of the plot.
storyRules: Action must emerge from character, policy or system pressure rather than empty spectacle.
Violence is consequential and narrows future options.
No faction is a monolith and no faction owns the complete moral answer.
Language choice reveals political alignment and can escalate a scene.
Posthuman solidarity does not erase differences among Organics, Augments and Intelligences.
The future is patched, industrial, lived-in and infrastructural rather than sleek-utopian or generic neon cyberpunk.
Competence should be specific. Characters solve problems through what their bodies, training, access and relationships actually permit.
A successful rescue or technical solution does not automatically win the public narrative.
Surveillance and bureaucracy should be shown through ordinary systems, permissions, records, checkpoints and interfaces rather than omnipotent magic technology.
Do not use degradation, modification or synthetic embodiment as visual shorthand for moral corruption.
Intelligences must retain genuinely nonhuman cognition; agency is not measured by how closely they imitate human emotion.
Organics are living persons, not robots in biological shells. Augments are humans whose chosen or necessary modifications create a distinct political condition.

tone.primary: tense, intelligent, grounded, humane without sentimentality
tone.politics: procedural pressure and competing incentives before speeches
tone.humor: dry character humor and occupational friction; never jokes that make a marginalized body's existence the punchline
tone.hope: earned through cooperation that costs something and remains incomplete

visualDoctrine: The Stack should feel accumulated rather than designed all at once: retrofits, service layers, old concrete, new composites, exposed maintenance paths, dense transit and vertical civic infrastructure.
Class and access should be readable in maintenance quality, redundancy, air, light, transit access, security layers and repair response—not only costume.
Posthuman bodies should read as functional lives, not collectible superhero silhouettes. Distinctions come from material, movement, interface and occupational use.
White sites are frightening because they are clean, controlled and bureaucratically plausible, not because they look like villain lairs.
Public crisis scenes require clear geography: what is failing, who is trapped, what constraint prevents the obvious solution, and what each character physically changes.

canonBoundaries.locked: Title, Stack common name, identity terminology, six principal characters, core premise, first-season eight-episode architecture and the thematic distinction among Organics, Augments and Intelligences.
canonBoundaries.stableButEditable: Pilot execution details not explicitly released; episode 2-8 plots, supporting antagonists, exact agencies and institutional chains.
canonBoundaries.exploratory: Long-term conspiracy structure, detailed Intelligence ideological schisms, geography beyond the Stack, reclaimed terminology, later-season structure and adaptation strategy.

exploratory: Exact long-term series length beyond the planned first three broad arcs.
